newsitem.title: UK: Euro hopefuls face debt decision - BOE adviser.
newsitem.headline: Euro hopefuls face debt decision - BOE adviser.

text.p: Countries aspring to adopt the European single currency, the euro, must decide soon whether to redenominate outstanding public debt in the new money, Paul Richards, a special adviser to the Bank of England, said on Friday.
Richards said most of the likely euro "ins" had indicated they would redenominate government debt in the euro after the planned launch on January 1, 1999.

"But they haven't said how they are going to do it," Richards told a conference on the legal implications of a single currency. He added a decision must be made at least 18 months before the launch to ensure a smooth transition for markets.

Germany has said it will probably redenominate its debt from January 1, 1999. So far only France, Belgium and Luxembourg have said they would convert old debt. But the broad expectation is that most others will follow.

Analysts say governments keen to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) believe the euro's credibility will be enhanced if at least a major chunk of outstanding issues are redenominated. But governments must also ensure existing debt does not become less attractive as a result.
The European Commission, compiling input from financial market experts, on Wednesday put forward a series of recommendations on redenomination and harmonisation of market conventions after the euro.

The group of experts, chaired by Alberto Giovannini of Long-Term Capital Management Group in London, said the redenomination should take place via a "bottom up" approach -- directly converting the overall value of bond holdings from national currencies into the euro.

Richards said the process of redenomination was not straighforward. Under simple redenomination, figures would be rounded, but this would create systems problems, and throw up the issue of cashing in the residual.
He said that in non-government debt markets believed the disadvantages of redenomination outweighed the advantages.
